outcome: Delivery modes (normal delivery, cesarean sections, instrumental deliveries)
Duration of first and second labor stages
cohort: The study included 30 low-risk singleton term pregnant women, aged 20-36 years, with gestational age >37 weeks, cephalic presentation, and ASA status I or II.
finding: Epidural analgesia was found to be a safe and effective method for labor pain management, providing substantial pain relief with favorable maternal and neonatal outcomes and no significant adverse effects on labor progression.
mod_finding: The study found no significant impact of epidural analgesia on the duration of the first and second stages of labor or on delivery modes, with 80% undergoing normal delivery, 16.67% cesarean sections, and 3.33% instrumental deliveries.
followup_time: Up to 5 minutes post-birth (for Apgar scores) and at delivery for other maternal and neonatal outcomes.
